scope: Practical, source-linked latency and generation-throughput snapshots for the exact provider/model set in data/model-pricing.json. Values describe specific first-party, marketplace, or cross-provider endpoints and must not be treated as intrinsic model constants.

definitions.timeToFirstTokenMs: Median milliseconds from request submission to the first generated token. For reasoning models that expose reasoning tokens, this is the first reasoning token.
definitions.timeToFirstTokenP95Ms: Milliseconds at or below which 95% of first-token observations fall.
definitions.outputTokensPerSecond: Median sustained output generation rate after the first token is received.
definitions.outputTokensPerSecondP95: 95th-percentile sustained output generation rate, only when the source defines the percentile direction clearly.
definitions.endToEndLatencyMs: Milliseconds from request submission until the complete response is received for the stated output length.
definitions.endToEndLatencyP95Ms: Milliseconds at or below which 95% of complete-response observations fall.
definitions.coldStartLatencyMs: Additional or total cold-start latency reported for an endpoint with scale-to-zero behavior.
definitions.cachedTimeToFirstTokenMs: Time to first token for a separately identified cached-input request.

methodology.summary: Numeric entries primarily use Artificial Analysis's independently measured default API workload. First-party models represent their first-party API; open-weight models without a first-party endpoint use the median across providers. OpenRouter-linked null records preserve coverage where no stable public measurement was available.

artificialAnalysisProfile.outputTokens: at least 1,500 for speed and TTFT runs
artificialAnalysisProfile.temperature: 0.6 for reasoning models; 0 for non-reasoning models unless provider-required

methodology.nullPolicy: Unavailable values are null, never zero. No estimates are included in this snapshot.
limitations: Latency changes with endpoint, region, request and response length, load, caching, service tier, routing, quantization, and sampling settings.
Artificial Analysis p50 values are rolling operational snapshots and can change within hours; lastUpdated is the retrieval date, not a promise of future performance.
Cross-provider median entries are useful model-level summaries but do not describe any single deployable endpoint.
Reasoning-model TTFT can mean time to the first reasoning token, not time to the first visible answer token.
End-to-end latency is only populated where the source supplies a response length; values for different output lengths are not comparable.
OpenRouter records with all-null metrics document current catalog coverage only; callers should not use them for ranking.
p95, cold-start, and cached-input measurements are rarely published consistently and remain null unless explicitly sourced.
